svg.text: ESP32-DevKitC (WROOM-32D) · dual VL53L0X (XSHUT) · water level · pump via MOSFET module · touch module · 0.96" OLED

g.text: which side goes to which rail
+ leg to 5V rail, − leg to GND · place near MOSFET module input

svg.text: RC filter with R3 — add only
MOSFET switches OUT− when SIG is HIGH
1. PUMP WIRING: the pump connects to exactly TWO wires — the MOSFET module's OUT+ and OUT− terminals. Nothing from the adapter touches the pump directly.
The adapter feeds only the module's INPUT terminals (VIN+ / VIN−). Inside the module, VIN+ passes straight through to OUT+, and the MOSFET connects OUT− to VIN− when SIG is HIGH.

2. CAPACITORS: C1 (1000µF electrolytic, POLARIZED) sits directly across the 5V and GND rails — + leg to 5V, − leg to GND, physically near the module input. Installing it backwards can make it vent/fail.
C2 (100nF ceramic) sits directly across the 3.3V and GND rails near the ESP32. Ceramic caps have no real polarity; the +/− marks only show which leg goes to which rail.
3. CONNECTION CONVENTION: a filled dot = wires are electrically connected. Lines that cross WITHOUT a dot are NOT connected — they just pass each other on the drawing.
4. D1 (1N4007) sits directly across the pump's two wires, cathode (banded end) toward OUT+. It absorbs the motor's inductive kickback when the MOSFET switches off.
5. R1 (100–220Ω) in series between GPIO26 and the module's SIG pin. R2 (10kΩ) from the SIG line down to GND — holds the gate LOW while the ESP32 boots so the pump can't glitch on.
6. I2C: all three devices (OLED 0x3C, sensor #1 0x30, sensor #2 0x29) share SDA=GPIO21 / SCL=GPIO22 at 100kHz (do NOT raise to 400kHz — verified unreliable with this wiring).
7. XSHUT boot sequence (firmware handles this): hold both XSHUT lines LOW → raise XSHUT1 (GPIO32) and reassign sensor #1 to 0x30 → raise XSHUT2 (GPIO33), sensor #2 keeps 0x29.
8. Touch module output is active-HIGH (HIGH = touched). Current minimal firmware has no touch code yet — when the module is added back, firmware must read HIGH as touched (no pull-up needed).
9. Before connecting any sensor: measure the 3.3V rail with a multimeter. It must read close to 3.3V and NEVER above 3.6V — an out-of-spec rail (3.7V) already killed one VL53L0X in this project.
10. Every wire in this drawing is a solid continuous line traced from source to destination. No dashed lines exist anywhere on this schematic.
11. TOUCH NOISE CONTROL: C3 (100nF ceramic) across the touch module's VCC/GND pins filters pump-PWM ripple from its supply — the touch IC false-triggers on noisy power. R3 (1kΩ series in the
SIG line) + C4 (100nF from SIG to GND) form an OPTIONAL RC filter — build without them first; add only if phantom touches appear. Physically place R3+C4 near the ESP32 end of the wire.
